inspiration.observed_pattern: A numbers relation joins each movie row to the positions represented in a comma-separated category string, while nested SUBSTRING_INDEX calls extract one category and CHAR_LENGTH minus REPLACE counts available delimiters.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored article-label report. The derived UNION ALL numbers relation expands at most five labels per article, the join predicate suppresses positions beyond each comma-separated list, and deterministic article/position ordering exposes each extracted label. The schema, rows, output columns, and reporting purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Articles 10, 20, and 30 contain three, one, and five labels respectively; article 40 has an empty label list and article 50 has NULL labels, so neither produces extracted rows. The numbers relation intentionally exposes positions one through five.
determinism_notes: The report orders by unique article ID and label position. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE articles (article_id INT PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, labels VARCHAR(255))

INSERT INTO articles VALUES (10, 'deploy guide', 'ops,api,db'), (20, 'release notes', 'draft'), (30, 'incident runbook', 'alert,triage,owner,mitigate,resolve'), (40, 'empty index', ''), (50, 'missing index', NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT a.article_id, a.title, n.position, SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(a.labels, ',', n.position), ',', -1) AS label FROM articles a INNER JOIN (SELECT 1 AS position UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5) n ON CHAR_LENGTH(a.labels) - CHAR_LENGTH(REPLACE(a.labels, ',', '')) >= n.position - 1 WHERE a.labels IS NOT NULL AND a.labels <> '' ORDER BY a.article_id, n.position

checks.sql: SELECT article_id, labels FROM articles WHERE article_id IN (40, 50) ORDER BY article_id
